headline: Prominent agent declares NHL expansion 'coming' to Houston and Atlanta
summary: Veteran player agent Allan Walsh publicly stated that 'NHL expansion is coming. Houston and Atlanta,' adding fuel to the league's 33rd-franchise race. The claim notably elevates Atlanta, which Commissioner Gary Bettman had said was not as far along as the Friedkin Group's Texas bid when the league opened its formal six-month expansion evaluation in June. A third Atlanta franchise would follow two failed NHL stints there, while any expansion bid is expected to require roughly $3.5 billion for a fee plus arena.

headline: Expansion race intensifies with Austin and Houston out front
summary: A month into the NHL's formal six-month evaluation of Texas expansion, Austin and Houston are described as leading the field for the league's 33rd franchise, ahead of Atlanta and a potential Arizona return. The Friedkin family holds exclusive negotiating rights in Texas under a Board of Governors-endorsed term sheet representing a roughly $3.5 billion commitment covering an expansion fee and a new arena in whichever market is chosen.

headline: NHL unveils first 84-game schedule as new CBA era begins
summary: The NHL set July 16 for the release of its full 2026-27 schedule, the first under the expanded 84-game regular-season format agreed in the CBA extension that takes effect this season, with opening-night matchups revealed a day earlier. The new CBA, ratified in July 2025 and running through 2029-30, also brings a playoff salary cap, shorter maximum contract terms and a four-game preseason limit, while the salary cap upper limit rises to $104 million for 2026-27.

headline: Rogers takes 100% of MLSE with C$4.35B buyout of Tanenbaum's 25%
summary: Rogers Communications agreed to buy the remaining 25% of Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment from Larry Tanenbaum's Kilmer Group for C$4.35 billion (about US$3.1 billion), valuing the parent of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Raptors at C$17.4 billion. The deal completes Rogers' consolidation of Canada's largest sports empire after its 2025 purchase of the Bell stake, and is expected to close in Q4 2026 pending league approvals — concentrating the Maple Leafs, national NHL media rights and Sportsnet under one owner.

headline: NHL Board of Governors unanimously approves $1.7B Penguins sale to Hoffmann family
summary: The Board of Governors unanimously approved Fenway Sports Group's sale of the Pittsburgh Penguins to the Hoffmann Family of Companies at an enterprise value of roughly $1.7-1.75 billion, the second-highest price ever for an NHL club behind the Tampa Bay Lightning's $1.8 billion sale in 2024. Geoff Hoffmann becomes governor, with Kyle Dubas among the alternate governors, and Commissioner Gary Bettman said the deal would close before the June 26 first round of the NHL Draft.

headline: NHL opens six-month expansion review of Houston and Austin with Friedkin family
summary: Following a Board of Governors meeting, Commissioner Gary Bettman announced a formal six-month process to evaluate Houston or Austin for a 33rd franchise, with billionaire Dan Friedkin's family as the prospective owner under a term sheet endorsed by the board's executive committee. The Friedkins' commitment is pegged at about $3.5 billion covering an expansion fee and construction of a new NHL arena, with Bettman noting Atlanta and Arizona remain interested but less advanced.
